            "text": "# AGENTS.md instructions\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n**You are running under Codex CLI.** Use Codex's own native tools for\nplanning, task tracking, and session recovery — here they are the\nstable, correct choice.\n\n> The OMP-native tool list (`todo_write`, `omp:sessions`, `goal`, `job`,\n> `checkpoint`/`rewind`, `search_tool_bm25`, `recipe`, `eval`, `irc`)\n> and the Claude task-panel tools (`TaskCreate`, `TaskList`, …) do not\n> exist in Codex — don't reach for them.\n\n- **Task tracking / planning** — use Codex's native plan tool\n  (`update_plan`, shown as the **Updated plan** panel) to maintain a\n  visible step list for any task with 3+ steps; keep it current as you\n  complete steps.\n- **Edits & shell** — use Codex's built-in `apply_patch` and shell tools\n  rather than inventing scratch files.\n- **Session recovery** — resume prior context with `codex resume`\n  (`--last` for the most recent); sessions live under\n  `$CODEX_HOME/sessions`. There is no `omp:sessions` equivalent to call.\n\nPapercusp coordination is the same on every client: use `coord:*` and\n`locks:*` (not a client-local tool) as the durable cross-session\nauthority for presence, handoffs, escalations, and file claims. For\ncompaction-sensitive work, write a successor brief naming the relevant\nplan/session state before context is summarized.\n\n**Finding a capability:** the ~550-tool catalog shows you only a seed. For a\ntool whose name you don't know, call `tools:find(\"<what you need>\")` (hybrid\nsearch over the full catalog), then call the returned tool directly.\n\nInside Codex `functions.exec`, Papercusp tools may be exposed as normalized\nJavaScript methods. Before calling a direct nested wrapper, check whether that\nexact method is callable, for example\n`typeof tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_find === \"function\"`. If it is callable,\nuse `tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_find({ query: \"<what you need>\" })` and\n`tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_invoke({ name, args })`; `tools.find` and\n`tools.invoke` are not aliases. A missing normalized method is a client exposure\ngap, not evidence the Papercusp capability is absent; use the CLI fallback below.\n\n**Your seeded tools are already callable. Do not re-find them after a restart.**\nThey are in `ALL_TOOLS` as `mcp__papercusp_su__<verb>` (`:`/`-` become `_`).\nCheck `ALL_TOOLS` first, then call the method directly:\n`tools.mcp__papercusp_su__work_items_get({ id, harness })`. Use `tools:find` only for a capability that is\nnot in `ALL_TOOLS`, or for argument keys its type omits; batch several in one query.\n\n**Codex MCP-deferral fallback:** never infer that a Papercusp capability\nis unavailable merely because its MCP schema is absent from the current\nmodel-facing tool list. If the whole `papercusp-su` namespace is missing,\nincluding `tools:find`, or the specific normalized wrapper you need is not\ncallable, use the installed CLI over the same MCP transport. Use `ptool\ntools:find` for discovery and `ptool tools:invoke` when the direct invoke\nwrapper is unavailable; `activated:false` means invoke the returned tool\nthrough `tools:invoke`, not that the tool is missing:\n\n**A direct wrapper returns `stale_tool_contract`?** The MCP session lacks a\n`tools/list` baseline for the current serving generation. Do not retry that\nwrapper or infer the capability is missing. Switch the affected work to the\n`ptool` CLI for this turn: each named `ptool` invocation opens its own MCP\nconnection and lists the current catalog before dispatch. `ptool --list` shows\nnames only; query `ptool tools:find` for an exact schema, then use\n`ptool tools:invoke` or the exact `ptool <group:verb>` call. The CLI uses its\nown connection, so it does not repair the old direct-wrapper session. Return\nto direct wrappers only after that client reconnects and refreshes its list.\n\n**A direct wrapper returns `native_tool_owner_unsupported_capability`?** The\nnative-owner route is refusing to forward a host-local `authenticatedPrincipal`\nacross the owner RPC; this preserves the authorization boundary. Treat it as a\ntransport refusal, not evidence that the tool is missing or its handler failed.\nDo NOT retry the same direct wrapper or route another `tools:invoke` call\nthrough that same native-owner path. Switch this and the remaining Papercusp\ncalls in the session to the installed `ptool` CLI, which opens its own\nauthenticated MCP connection and retains this session's `PAPERCUSP_SID`: use\n`ptool tools:find` for schema, then `ptool <group:verb>` or `ptool\ntools:invoke`. A successful ptool call verifies the CLI route only; it does not\nprove the native wrapper route is healthy and is not a reason to loosen\n`authenticatedPrincipal` forwarding.\n\nWhen you call `exec_command` through `functions.exec`, remember that the outer\nprogram is JavaScript. **Never put a shell command containing `${...}` inside a\nJavaScript template literal**: V8 resolves it before `exec_command` starts, so a\nshell variable such as `${PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE}` becomes a JavaScript\n`ReferenceError`. Keep that command in a normal JavaScript string, or escape the\ndollar sign as `\\${...}` when a template literal is genuinely necessary.\nThe same boundary bites REGEX metacharacters: every layer between your JS source\nand rg's parser adds one phantom escape (`'^\\\\\\\\{'` reaches rg as `^\\\\\\\\{` and is\nrejected as `repetition quantifier expects a valid decimal`). For LITERAL braces\nuse `rg -n -F '{'` and DROP the anchors (`-F` treats `^` literally too), or keep\nexactly ONE backslash in a single-quoted shell literal (`rg -n -o '^\\{'`).\n\n```bash\nptool_scope=(--workspace=\"${PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE}\")\nif [[ -n \"${PAPERCUSP_HARNESS_SLUG:-}\" ]]; then\n  ptool_scope+=(--harness=\"${PAPERCUSP_HARNESS_SLUG}\")\nfi\nptool tools:find --json - \"${ptool_scope[@]}\" <<'JSON'\n{\"query\":\"<what you need — or an exact verb name, to read that verb's schema>\"}\nJSON\n```\n\nEach hit carries an **`argSchema`** — the tool's exact accepted keys — not just a\nname. **Read it before any write call, and copy the keys from it.** Guessing\nintuitive argument names is the single most common way a mutation fails here,\nand it costs a retry round trip every time: `locks:acquire` takes `paths` (NOT\n`files`, and it accepts no `harness` — it is workspace-global);\n`improvements:capture` takes `body` (NOT `description` or `evidence`). `ptool\n--list` shows names and descriptions only, so on the `ptool` path it cannot\nanswer this — there, querying `tools:find` for a verb you already know by name\nis the schema lookup.\n\nThen call it with quoting-safe stdin JSON, keys taken from that `argSchema`:\n\n```bash\nptool <group:verb> --json - <<'JSON'\n{...}\nJSON\n```\n\nUse `--json-file` when a payload is easier as a file. Never put arbitrary JSON\nin shell single quotes: one apostrophe breaks the shell before `ptool` runs.\n(`ptool tools:invoke` also works.) `ptool` keeps this session's\n`PAPERCUSP_SID`, so claims and audit attribution stay yours. It is the\nsanctioned escape hatch when Codex defers every MCP tool, not evidence the\nserver or capability is missing.\n\n## An empty `exec_command` result means YIELDED, not failed — pass `yield_time_ms: 30000`\n\n`exec_command` **yields at 10 seconds by default** (`yield_time_ms`, range 250–30000 ms).\nOn yield it returns *whatever has been emitted so far* — for a `ptool` call, which buffers its\nJSON and writes it in one shot at the end, that is **zero bytes** — and hands back a\n`session_id` while your command **keeps running**. Nothing is killed and nothing is lost.\n\n**Pick by how long the call might take — the two remedies have different ceilings:**\n\n- **Under ~30s (the common case): pass `yield_time_ms: 30000`.** One call, no extra steps.\n  Covers `coord:orient`, `plans:get`, `work_items:list`, `release:trace`, `tools:invoke` and\n  every `ptool` invocation above. This is a fix, not a workaround.\n- **Unknown duration, or possibly over 30s: use two-call file capture** (below). `yield_time_ms`\n  is capped at **30000 ms — a hard maximum, not headroom** — so it raises the yield boundary\n  rather than removing i… [truncated 182584 chars]"

            "text": "# AGENTS.md instructions\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n**You are running under Codex CLI.** Use Codex's own native tools for\nplanning, task tracking, and session recovery — here they are the\nstable, correct choice.\n\n> The OMP-native tool list (`todo_write`, `omp:sessions`, `goal`, `job`,\n> `checkpoint`/`rewind`, `search_tool_bm25`, `recipe`, `eval`, `irc`)\n> and the Claude task-panel tools (`TaskCreate`, `TaskList`, …) do not\n> exist in Codex — don't reach for them.\n\n- **Task tracking / planning** — use Codex's native plan tool\n  (`update_plan`, shown as the **Updated plan** panel) to maintain a\n  visible step list for any task with 3+ steps; keep it current as you\n  complete steps.\n- **Edits & shell** — use Codex's built-in `apply_patch` and shell tools\n  rather than inventing scratch files.\n- **Session recovery** — resume prior context with `codex resume`\n  (`--last` for the most recent); sessions live under\n  `$CODEX_HOME/sessions`. There is no `omp:sessions` equivalent to call.\n\nPapercusp coordination is the same on every client: use `coord:*` and\n`locks:*` (not a client-local tool) as the durable cross-session\nauthority for presence, handoffs, escalations, and file claims. For\ncompaction-sensitive work, write a successor brief naming the relevant\nplan/session state before context is summarized.\n\n**Finding a capability:** the ~550-tool catalog shows you only a seed. For a\ntool whose name you don't know, call `tools:find(\"<what you need>\")` (hybrid\nsearch over the full catalog), then call the returned tool directly.\n\nInside Codex `functions.exec`, Papercusp tools may be exposed as normalized\nJavaScript methods. Before calling a direct nested wrapper, check whether that\nexact method is callable, for example\n`typeof tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_find === \"function\"`. If it is callable,\nuse `tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_find({ query: \"<what you need>\" })` and\n`tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_invoke({ name, args })`; `tools.find` and\n`tools.invoke` are not aliases. A missing normalized method is a client exposure\ngap, not evidence the Papercusp capability is absent; use the CLI fallback below.\n\n**Your seeded tools are already callable. Do not re-find them after a restart.**\nThey are in `ALL_TOOLS` as `mcp__papercusp_su__<verb>` (`:`/`-` become `_`).\nCheck `ALL_TOOLS` first, then call the method directly:\n`tools.mcp__papercusp_su__work_items_get({ id, harness })`. Use `tools:find` only for a capability that is\nnot in `ALL_TOOLS`, or for argument keys its type omits; batch several in one query.\n\n**Codex MCP-deferral fallback:** never infer that a Papercusp capability\nis unavailable merely because its MCP schema is absent from the current\nmodel-facing tool list. Return\nto direct wrappers only after that client reconnects and refreshes its list.\n\n**A direct wrapper returns `native_tool_owner_unsupported_capability`?** The\nnative-owner route is refusing to forward a host-local `authenticatedPrincipal`\nacross the owner RPC; this preserves the authorization boundary. Treat it as a\ntransport refusal, not evidence that the tool is missing or its handler failed.\nDo NOT retry the same direct wrapper or route another `tools:invoke` call\nthrough that same native-owner path. Switch this and the remaining Papercusp\ncalls in the session to the installed `ptool` CLI, which opens its own\nauthenticated MCP connection and retains this session's `PAPERCUSP_SID`: use\n`ptool tools:find` for schema, then `ptool <group:verb>` or `ptool\ntools:invoke`. A successful ptool call verifies the CLI route only; it does not\nprove the native wrapper route is healthy and is not a reason to loosen\n`authenticatedPrincipal` forwarding.\n\nWhen you call `exec_command` through `functions.exec`, remember that the outer\nprogram is JavaScript. **Never put a shell command containing `${...}` inside a\nJavaScript template literal**: V8 resolves it before `exec_command` starts, so a\nshell variable such as `${PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE}` becomes a JavaScript\n`ReferenceError`. A `detached: true` spawn creates a\\nprocess meant to **outlive the call that made it** — the root of a subtree — so it must be\\nenrolled in the task ledger: **`managedSpawn`** (`task-manager/managed-spawn.ts`) for an\\nasync seam, **`beginSyncEnrolment` + `completeSyncEnrolment` + `finishSyncEnrolment`**\\n(`task-manager/enroll-sync.ts`) for a sync one. `lint:no-unenrolled-spawn` fails a new\\nun-enrolled site; genuinely-not-ours lifetimes (a human terminal window, a pre-operator\\nbootstrap, a release cut that survives the restart it performs) go in that guard's\\nALLOWLIST **with a reason**. Ordinary short-lived spawns need nothing — cgroup membership\\nis inherited, so a `git rev-parse` inside an already-confined process is already accounted\\nfor. That inheritance is the whole design: confine the ROOTS, and the kernel accounts for\\nevery descendant, including ones that double-fork and reparent to init.\\n\\n⛔ **Never kill by name or pattern.** `pkill -f '<binary>'` has twice killed the owner's\\nlive desktop window and peer agents' Xvfb instances. Use **`processes:kill { taskId }`** —\\nit kills the whole cgroup subtree and cannot reach a recycled pid (PID wrap happens ~daily\\nhere under fleet load). An `identity_mismatch` refusal is the rail working, not a bug. To\\nrelieve pressure without losing work, **`processes:freeze`** beats killing.\\n\\n| you want | use | not |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| what is running AND WHY (who launched it, for which work-item, what it costs) | `processes:list` | `ps`/`pgrep` — kernel-shaped, zero provenance |\\n| the six tracked AGENT process kinds | `dev:processes` (unchanged, deliberately narrow) | `processes:list` |\\n| a real whole-host process list | plain `ps`/`pgrep` (never gated) | `processes:list` — it will answer wrong, not empty |\\n\\nHuman pane: `/admin/tasks` (sibling of `/admin/schedules` — that one inventories everything\\nRECURRING, this one everything RUNNING). Full model:\\n[the task manager and the no-escape property](/internal/docs/agent-insights/task-manager-and-the-no-escape-property).\\n\\n## Shared-lib singletons: pin through the primitive, never by hand\\n\\nModule-scoped mutable state in a shared package (`const registry = new Map()`, a cache,\\na pool, a `configure*()` host-seam object) is a singleton **only if the loader produces\\nexactly one module record**. Several ordinary seams break that with no error: tsx's CJS\\npreflight beside the ESM loader, the same file reached by bare specifier and by relative\\npath, `node_modules/@papercusp/*` symlinked into the repo, a bundled copy beside source.\\nWhen it splits, each record gets its own state and writes to one are invisible to readers\\nof the other. Nothing throws — you get a *partial* view that looks complete.\\n\\n**Use `pinModuleState` from `@papercusp/module-singleton`, at module scope, once:**\\n\\n```ts\\nconst state = pinModuleState('@papercusp/your-pkg.state', () => ({ registry: new Map() }));\\n```\\n\\nIt pins to `globalThis` under a `Symbol.for` key — correct under *every* seam above, so\\nyou never have to prove which one applies — and counts evaluations, so a re-split is\\nreported by `listModuleDuplications()` instead of being rediscovered the expensive way.\\n⚠ **Do not hand-roll the `Symbol.for` + `globalThis` pair.** Hand-rolling still fixes\\ncorrectness, but the key is invisible to the central report, which then answers a\\nconfident `[]` while your module is split — the failure below, one level up.\\n**`npm run lint:no-hand-rolled-module-pin` fails on a new one** (and\\n`-- --list` prints the full measured population, which is how its allowlist is\\nre-seeded — never from a hand-run grep).\\n\\n## Deployment model: desktop is the product; the standalone webapp is RETIRED\\n\\nShipping target = the Tauri desktop app; **SSE is the sync path that matters** —\\n`HarnessSyncProvider` passes a literal `syncType=\\\"SSE\\\"` with **no** runtime\\nbranch, so a plain browser tab runs the SAME transport as production.                   "text": "Script completed\nWall time 1.9 seconds\nOutput:\n\n{\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"{\\\"advisory\\\":\\\"⚠ single-agent activity read: harness_shared.tool_invocations records MCP calls ONLY, so this window is NOT \\\\\\\"everything this agent did\\\\\\\" — native Claude Code Bash/Read/Grep/Edit produce no row at all, and this box's bypass-permissions preamble actively steers agents to native Bash for reads. Measured over ingested transcript parts (24h): native 54,009 calls across 183 agents vs MCP 35,479 across 128, so ~60% of recorded tool use is invisible here. The error is DIRECTIONAL — missing rows can only make an agent look LESS active, so a sparse or empty window reads as \\\\\\\"idle\\\\\\\" and escalates into waking, accusing or reassigning a peer who was working (EI-21847759967934033: this ledger showed one agent making only coord:glance / activity:report while it was in fact running Bash the whole time). THE RULE: positive rows prove activity; absence here proves nothing.             "text": "# AGENTS.md instructions\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n**You are running under Codex CLI.** Use Codex's own native tools for\nplanning, task tracking, and session recovery — here they are the\nstable, correct choice.\n\n> The OMP-native tool list (`todo_write`, `omp:sessions`, `goal`, `job`,\n> `checkpoint`/`rewind`, `search_tool_bm25`, `recipe`, `eval`, `irc`)\n> and the Claude task-panel tools (`TaskCreate`, `TaskList`, …) do not\n> exist in Codex — don't reach for them.\n\n- **Task tracking / planning** — use Codex's native plan tool\n  (`update_plan`, shown as the **Updated plan** panel) to maintain a\n  visible step list for any task with 3+ steps; keep it current as you\n  complete steps.\n- **Edits & shell** — use Codex's built-in `apply_patch` and shell tools\n  rather than inventing scratch files.\n- **Session recovery** — resume prior context with `codex resume`\n  (`--last` for the most recent); sessions live under\n  `$CODEX_HOME/sessions`. There is no `omp:sessions` equivalent to call.\n\nPapercusp coordination is the same on every client: use `coord:*` and\n`locks:*` (not a client-local tool) as the durable cross-session\nauthority for presence, handoffs, escalations, and file claims. For\ncompaction-sensitive work, write a successor brief naming the relevant\nplan/session state before context is summarized.\n\n**Finding a capability:** the ~550-tool catalog shows you only a seed. For a\ntool whose name you don't know, call `tools:find(\"<what you need>\")` (hybrid\nsearch over the full catalog), then call the returned tool directly.\n\nInside Codex `functions.exec`, Papercusp tools may be exposed as normalized\nJavaScript methods. Before calling a direct nested wrapper, check whether that\nexact method is callable, for example\n`typeof tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_find === \"function\"`. If it is callable,\nuse `tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_find({ query: \"<what you need>\" })` and\n`tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_invoke({ name, args })`; `tools.find` and\n`tools.invoke` are not aliases. A missing normalized method is a client exposure\ngap, not evidence the Papercusp capability is absent; use the CLI fallback below.\n\n**Your seeded tools are already callable. Do not re-find them after a restart.**\nThey are in `ALL_TOOLS` as `mcp__papercusp_su__<verb>` (`:`/`-` become `_`).\nCheck `ALL_TOOLS` first, then call the method directly:\n`tools.mcp__papercusp_su__work_items_get({ id, harness })`. Use `tools:find` only for a capability that is\nnot in `ALL_TOOLS`, or for argument keys its type omits; batch several in one query.\n\n**Codex MCP-deferral fallback:** never infer that a Papercusp capability\nis unavailable merely because its MCP schema is absent from the current\nmodel-facing tool list. If the whole `papercusp-su` namespace is missing,\nincluding `tools:find`, or the specific normalized wrapper you need is not\ncallable, use the installed CLI over the same MCP transport. Use `ptool\ntools:find` for discovery and `ptool tools:invoke` when the direct invoke\nwrapper is unavailable; `activated:false` means invoke the returned tool\nthrough `tools:invoke`, not that the tool is missing:\n\n**A direct wrapper returns `stale_tool_contract`?** The MCP session lacks a\n`tools/list` baseline for the current serving generation. Do not retry that\nwrapper or infer the capability is missing. Switch the affected work to the\n`ptool` CLI for this turn: each named `ptool` invocation opens its own MCP\nconnection and lists the current catalog before dispatch. `ptool --list` shows\nnames only; query `ptool tools:find` for an exact schema, then use\n`ptool tools:invoke` or the exact `ptool <group:verb>` call. The CLI uses its\nown connection, so it does not repair the old direct-wrapper session. Return\nto direct wrappers only after that client reconnects and refreshes its list.\n\n**A direct wrapper returns `native_tool_owner_unsupported_capability`?** The\nnative-owner route is refusing to forward a host-local `authenticatedPrincipal`\nacross the owner RPC; this preserves the authorization boundary. Treat it as a\ntransport refusal, not evidence that the tool is missing or its handler failed.\nDo NOT retry the same direct wrapper or route another `tools:invoke` call\nthrough that same native-owner path. Switch this and the remaining Papercusp\ncalls in the session to the installed `ptool` CLI, which opens its own\nauthenticated MCP connection and retains this session's `PAPERCUSP_SID`: use\n`ptool tools:find` for schema, then `ptool <group:verb>` or `ptool\ntools:invoke`. A successful ptool call verifies the CLI route only; it does not\nprove the native wrapper route is healthy and is not a reason to loosen\n`authenticatedPrincipal` forwarding.\n\nWhen you call `exec_command` through `functions.exec`, remember that the outer\nprogram is JavaScript. **Never put a shell command containing `${...}` inside a\nJavaScript template literal**: V8 resolves it before `exec_command` starts, so a\nshell variable such as `${PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE}` becomes a JavaScript\n`ReferenceError`. Keep that command in a normal JavaScript string, or escape the\ndollar sign as `\\${...}` when a template literal is genuinely necessary.\nThe same boundary bites REGEX metacharacters: every layer between your JS source\nand rg's parser adds one phantom escape (`'^\\\\\\\\{'` reaches rg as `^\\\\\\\\{` and is\nrejected as `repetition quantifier expects a valid decimal`). Keep mem0 entries SHORT, and when\\n    the why already lives in a doc/plan store only the non-derivable fact + a POINTER\\n    (`[[<plan-slug>]]`, `/internal/docs/agent-insights/<slug>`), never a copied paragraph.\\n  - **In-flight state** → coord; **derivable session state** (X shipped, migration N, N tests)\\n    → the plan / work-item, never memory.\\nSee the plans `papercusp-su-memory-2026-05-25` and\\n`tool-call-batching-wrappers-2026-06-21`.\\n\\n## Your tool surface is DYNAMIC — the whole 959-tool catalog is reachable on demand\\n\\nYour loaded tool list is usually a small CORE set (the default). Any tool NOT in it is still\\nreachable — you do not need everything loaded up front:\\n- **`tools:find(\\\"<what you want to do>\\\")`** — intent search; matched tools are activated so you can call them directly next.\\n- **`tools:invoke({ name, args })`** — call ANY tool by exact name without loading it (the universal fallback).\\nWhen you need a capability that isn't in your loaded set, SEARCH for it — don't assume it doesn't exist.\\n⚠ Your CLIENT's own tool search (Claude Code ToolSearch, OMP search_tool_bm25) indexes ONLY this\\nadvertised subset — a zero-hit search THERE does NOT mean the tool doesn't exist (EI-9011: agents\\nhit this and degraded to polling). Any tool name you read in an error message, hook text, doc, or\\npeer message is callable RIGHT NOW via `tools:invoke { name, args }`, and `tools:find` searches the\\nFULL server-side catalog regardless of what your client advertises.\\nIf a found tool still errors \\\"not found\\\" when called directly, run it via `tools:invoke` — never guess alternative names.\\n\\nCapability map — the Full model:\\n[the task manager and the no-escape property](/internal/docs/agent-insights/task-manager-and-the-no-escape-property).\\n\\n## Shared-lib singletons: pin through the primitive, never by hand\\n\\nModule-scoped mutable state in a shared package (`const registry = new Map()`, a cache,\\na pool, a `configure*()` host-seam object) is a singleton **only if the loader produces\\nexactly one module record**.             "text": "Script completed\nWall time 1.9 seconds\nOutput:\n\n{\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"{\\\"advisory\\\":\\\"⚠ single-agent activity read: harness_shared.tool_invocations records MCP calls ONLY, so this window is NOT \\\\\\\"everything this agent did\\\\\\\" — native Claude Code Bash/Read/Grep/Edit produce no row at all, and this box's bypass-permissions preamble actively steers agents to native Bash for reads. Measured over ingested transcript parts (24h): native 54,009 calls across 183 agents vs MCP 35,479 across 128, so ~60% of recorded tool use is invisible here. The error is DIRECTIONAL — missing rows can only make an agent look LESS active, so a sparse or empty window reads as \\\\\\\"idle\\\\\\\" and escalates into waking, accusing or reassigning a peer who was working (EI-21847759967934033: this ledger showed one agent making only coord:glance / activity:report while it was in fact running Bash the whole time). THE RULE: positive rows prove activity; absence here proves nothing. To look for the missing half, start with `activity:tool-log { owner: '<the coord ownerId>' }` — it reads harness_shared.agent_activity, which DOES record native calls, and renders the command text. But do not invert the error onto it: that store is empty for ~45% of agents (24h: 182 of 333 tool_invocations owners had any rows), so an empty tool-log is equally not evidence of idleness. Corroborate with the transcript store, which is corpus-namespaced — workspace_id = 'default', NOT your tenant id: SELECT ts, tool_name, text FROM harness_shared.session_turn_parts WHERE workspace_id = 'default' AND owner = '<the coord ownerId>' AND ts > now() - interval '30 minutes' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50. `owner` is the coord ownerId and `text` is the faithful-render payload column, so both take the same id you scoped this query with. ⚠ tenant scope: harness_shared.tool_invocations (keyed by workspace_id + harness_slug) — multi-tenant, but this filtered query has no workspace_id/harness_slug predicate — a bare slug/id filter can silently match ANOTHER tenant's rows and read as stale/diverged state. Add: workspace_id = 'papercusp-workspace' AND harness_slug = 'papercusp'.
